references.text: Three times a year all Israelite men were to go up to the Lord to celebrate the major festivals. Jesus follows this command by going up to Jerusalem for one of the Jewish feasts ([ref:2 Mos 23:14-17|Exodus 23:14-17]).
The command that all men must appear before the Lord three times a year is repeated here. Jesus' journey up to Jerusalem for the feast aligns with this ([ref:2 Mos 34:23|Exodus 34:23]).

Three times a year all men shall appear before the face of the Lord at the place he chooses – providing background for why Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for the feast ([ref:5 Mos 16:16|Deuteronomy 16:16]).
Here too, Jesus goes up to Jerusalem in connection with the Jewish Passover. John repeatedly tells of Jesus' journeys to Jerusalem for the feasts ([ref:Joh 2:13|John 2:13]).
The Galileans welcomed Jesus because they had seen everything he did in Jerusalem during the feast. This provides context for Jesus' return to Jerusalem in 5:1 ([ref:Joh 4:45|John 4:45]).
John notes that Passover, the Jewish feast, was near. This is one of several feast references in the gospel that structure the narrative, similar to the unnamed feast in 5:1 ([ref:Joh 6:4|John 6:4]).

Another reference to one of the Jewish feasts (the Feast of Tabernacles) which Jesus then goes up to Jerusalem to attend. John consistently uses the feasts as a structuring element ([ref:Joh 7:2|John 7:2]).
Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for the Feast of Tabernacles, forming a pattern with 5:1 where Jesus repeatedly travels to Jerusalem to participate in Jewish feasts ([ref:Joh 7:10|John 7:10]).
The Jewish Passover was near, and many went up to Jerusalem. Jesus again goes up for a feast in Jerusalem, as in 5:1 ([ref:Joh 11:55|John 11:55]).
